primitives.name: Weighted Stolen Base Runs
primitives.verbatim_quote: Goal Determine the impact of baserunning on an MLB team's ability to win baseball games. BsR
primitives.assumptions: Assumes linear value contribution from stolen bases, Ultimate Base Running, and ground into double play prevention.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when defensive shifts dramatically alter steal success rates.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's situational win probability framework where each component contributes to expected marginal gains. In GSE, it informs state-transition probabilities between base-out states.
layer2.telemetry: Observed change in team win probability per successful stolen base attempt.

primitives.name: Ultimate Base Running
primitives.verbatim_quote: Goal Determine the impact of baserunning on an MLB team's ability to win baseball games. BsR
primitives.assumptions: Standardizes running efficiency relative to league average, accounting for park factors and pitcher handedness.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when small sample sizes introduce significant noise in individual player estimates.

layer2.mapping: Used in GSI's conformal prediction intervals for player performance. In GSE, it drives tactical decisions on aggressive versus conservative baserunning.
layer2.telemetry: Average runs saved per 100 at-bats above league average.

The core insight is that baserunning efficiency translates directly into marginal runs, which compound into wins. The primitives decompose total base-running impact into its constituent parts: stolen base success, general running efficiency, and preventing double-plays. Each component carries distinct statistical properties—wSB is highly volatile, UBR adjusts for context, and wGDP addresses a specific negative outcome. The failure mode occurs when defensive strategies (shifts, pitch-tunneling) systematically alter the underlying transition probabilities assumed by these metrics. For GSI, this requires conformal prediction intervals around predicted runs. For GSE, it demands state-based reasoning where the optimal action depends on the current base-out situation and pitcher tendencies.
